name: United States
summary: In the USA, lamps and retro-reflectors are governed by FMVSS No. 108 (49 CFR 571.108). There is no type approval: the manufacturer self-certifies compliance (49 U.S.C. 30115), and UN/ECE approvals are not recognised – a rear lamp built to ECE rules may only be sold once its functions are certified to FMVSS 108. Passenger cars also need red side marker lamps and red side retro-reflectors at the rear; plastic lenses require 3 years of outdoor weathering in Florida and Arizona.

standards.title: Lamps, reflective devices, and associated equipment
standards.scope: Original and replacement lamps, retro-reflectors and associated equipment for passenger cars, MPVs, trucks, buses, trailers and motorcycles (S1, S3). Table I-a sets number, colour, location, mounting height and activation for the tail lamp (S7.2), stop lamp (S7.3), side marker lamp (S7.4), reversing lamp (S7.6), high-mounted stop lamp (S7.9) and retro-reflector (S8.1). Colour testing and testing of plastic optical materials in S14.4, mechanical and environmental tests in S14.5.

standards.title: Certification of compliance (Vehicle Safety Act)
standards.scope: Legal basis for self-certification: the manufacturer certifies that the vehicle or equipment item meets all applicable FMVSS and must exercise 'reasonable care' in doing so (as summarised in the NHTSA manufacturer handbook).

standards.title: Service of Process on Foreign Manufacturers and Importers
standards.scope: Foreign manufacturers, assemblers and importers of vehicles or equipment must appoint an agent for service of process based in the USA.

standards.title: Manufacturer Identification
standards.scope: Manufacturers of vehicles and of equipment covered by an FMVSS must submit information about themselves and a description of their products to NHTSA no later than 30 days after production starts (per the NHTSA handbook).

standards.title: Defect and noncompliance information report
standards.scope: Report to NHTSA on every safety-related defect and every noncompliance with an FMVSS in original or replacement equipment, no later than 5 working days after it is determined.

certification.marking: For signal lamps and retro-reflectors, the 'DOT' symbol is optional (FMVSS 108 S6.5.1.2: 'may be marked'). If used, the marking counts as certification of compliance with FMVSS 108. According to the NHTSA handbook, certification is usually shown with 'DOT' on the part or on the shipping container. DOT marking on the lens is mandatory only for headlamps (S6.5.1).
certification.summary: No type approval and no certification by an authority: NHTSA does not issue type approvals and does not certify vehicles or equipment. The manufacturer self-certifies compliance with FMVSS 108 (49 U.S.C. 30115) and must exercise 'reasonable care', in practice through its own or commissioned tests following the standard's test procedures. Before placing on the market, the following are needed: a US agent for service of process for foreign manufacturers (Part 551 Subpart D) and the manufacturer identification submission to NHTSA (Part 566, no later than 30 days after production starts). After that, recall and reporting obligations apply (Part 573: report within 5 working days). NHTSA checks compliance after the fact.

deviations.topic: Self-certification to FMVSS 108 instead of UN approval
deviations.national_requirement: Equipment that does not meet all applicable FMVSS may not be imported or sold. According to an NHTSA interpretation (letter to Hella, 1998), a rear lamp that meets the ECE requirements for passenger cars counts as 'motor vehicle equipment'. It may only be sold once the manufacturer has certified that all lamp functions comply with FMVSS 108. NHTSA does not grant type approval. The manufacturer self-certifies under 49 U.S.C. 30115 and must exercise 'reasonable care' in doing so.
deviations.suggestion: Create an FMVSS 108 compliance file for each function (tail, stop and reversing lamp as well as retro-reflector), with test reports per S14 (photometry, colour, plastic optics, vibration, humidity, dust, corrosion). Do not rely on the E approval for this.

deviations.topic: Rear side marker lamp and rear side retro-reflector (red)
deviations.national_requirement: FMVSS 108 Table I-a requires every passenger car to have one red side marker lamp per side, as far to the rear as practicable (mounting height at least 15 in, approx. 381 mm). It must be switched on together with the headlamps or parking lamps. In addition, one red side retro-reflector per side (15–60 in, approx. 381–1524 mm). Photometry: Table X (red, at least 0.25 cd at the test points) and Table XVI-a respectively.
deviations.suggestion: Add a red side marker lamp and a red side retro-reflector to the rear lamp, both facing the side of the vehicle. Alternatively, agree with the vehicle manufacturer that both functions are located elsewhere on the vehicle, and document this in the specification.

deviations.topic: Photometry and stop-to-tail lamp ratio per FMVSS 108
deviations.national_requirement: Photometry is demonstrated at the test points of the FMVSS tables: Table VIII (tail lamp), Table IX (stop lamp), Table XII (reversing lamp), Table XVI-a (retro-reflector; red at least 420 mcd/lux at 0.2° observation and 0° entrance angle), each per S14.2. If the tail lamp is combined with the stop lamp, the stop lamp must reach at least the tail lamp's luminous intensity times the factor from Table IX at every test point (S7.3.12). Dual-filament bulbs require an indexed base and an indexed socket (S7.3.15).
deviations.suggestion: Measure the photometry of all functions at the FMVSS test points (Tables VIII, IX, XII, XVI-a), demonstrate the stop-to-tail lamp ratio per S7.3.12 point by point, and add both to the specification. For dual-filament bulbs, use an indexed base.

deviations.topic: Plastic optical materials: 3 years of outdoor weathering in Florida and Arizona
deviations.national_requirement: Every plastic material used for optical parts (coated and uncoated) needs 3 years of outdoor weathering in Florida and Arizona. Accelerated weathering is not permitted (S14.4.2). Sample thicknesses: 1.6, 2.3, 3.2 and 6.4 mm. Limits after weathering: haze or loss of gloss at most 30 % for outer lenses and at most 7 % for retro-reflectors and lenses in front of retro-reflectors; luminous transmittance changes by at most 25 %; no colour bleeding, crazing or cracking; colour requirement still met. Plus a heat test: 2 h at 79 ± 3 °C.
deviations.suggestion: Request evidence from the PMMA supplier of 3 years of outdoor weathering in Florida and Arizona per FMVSS 108 S14.4.2, for the red grade or colour formulation and wall thickness used. Otherwise, allow 3 years of lead time for the weathering. Add the evidence to the material specification.

deviations.topic: DOT marking and manufacturer registration with NHTSA
deviations.national_requirement: Signal lamps and retro-reflectors may be marked 'DOT'. This then counts as certification of compliance with FMVSS 108 (S6.5.1.2, optional). According to the NHTSA handbook, certification is usually shown with 'DOT' on the part or on the shipping container. An E mark has no certification effect in the USA. Foreign manufacturers must appoint a US agent for service of process before selling (49 CFR Part 551 Subpart D) and register with NHTSA no later than 30 days after production starts (49 CFR Part 566).
deviations.suggestion: Add the 'DOT' marking on the lens in the tool, or alternatively on the packaging. Appoint a US agent for service of process under Part 551 and submit the manufacturer identification under Part 566 via the NHTSA Manufacturer Portal.

deviations.topic: Minimum lit area of the stop lamp
deviations.national_requirement: Stop lamps on passenger cars (vehicle width under 2032 mm) need an effective projected luminous lens area of at least 5000 mm² if they have only one compartment. With several compartments or lamps, at least 2200 mm² per compartment and 5000 mm² in total are required (FMVSS 108 S6.4.1, Table IV-a).
deviations.suggestion: Design the effective lit area of the stop lamp function to at least 5000 mm² (with several compartments, at least 2200 mm² per compartment) and demonstrate this in the specification.
